title: Subject–Verb Agreement

explanation.en: In the simple present, he, she, and it usually take -s or -es. I, you, we, and they generally use the base verb.
explanation.taglish: Kapag he, she, o it, usually may -s o -es sa simple present. Base verb sa I, you, we, at they. Halimbawa: She works on Mondays.
explanation.fil: Sa simple present, madalas may -s o -es ang pandiwa kapag he, she, o it ang simuno.

exercises.explanation: Add -s or -es to most simple-present verbs. Correct answer: She works here.
Use the base form in ordinary simple-present statements. Correct answer: work
exercises.hint: Decide whether the sentence is simple present.

exercises.explanation: Use am, is, or are depending on the subject. Correct answer: He sends reports.
Use am, is, or are depending on the subject. Correct answer: I am ready.
Use am, is, or are depending on the subject. Correct answer: My manager reviews the plan.

writing.prompt: Write one sentence about what a colleague usually does.
writing.exampleAnswer: My colleague sends updates every Monday.
